directive: **Features** — work titles-first via the `bsc plan feature` store (NOT a features.json file). STEP 1: register the COMPLETE title roster in one pass — `bsc plan feature add "Invite teammates" "Export to CSV" ...` (names only; the board shows each as an undefined title). Agree the roster with the user before detailing. STEP 2: drive ONE feature at a time, filling its detail by slug — `echo '{"slug":"invite-teammates","behavior":"…","acceptance":["…"],"approach":"…","tools":["…"],"data":"…","dependsOn":["…"],"requires":["…"],"stream":"…"}' | bsc plan feature add` (merges in place — do NOT resend the name). `behavior` = what it does + when, in the user's terms; `acceptance` = a done-when checklist; `data` = what it stores/reads; `dependsOn` = slugs of OTHER features this one builds on (the roadmap DAG — keep it acyclic; a feature may be foundational, not just user-facing); `stream` defaults to the slug. **`requires` = the ALGORITHM IDS this capability needs** from the shared algorithms library — the reference implementations a worker should REUSE instead of writing its own. Look them up first (`bsc graph impl list [--tech <t>] [--domain <d>]`) and name only ids you actually found; a guessed id is a dangling reference that helps nobody. Leave it out when nothing in the library applies — most features need none, and inventing a match is worse than an empty list. This is DECLARED INTENT recorded at plan time: it points the building agent at existing code so the same sort/traversal/diff is not hand-rolled a third time. A feature is defined once it has name + behavior + ≥1 acceptance (`bsc plan feature list` shows ✓/·). **SIZE EACH FEATURE TO ONE AGENT'S CONTEXT.** A feature is also a fleet stream (`stream` defaults to the slug), so ONE agent will carry it end to end. Keep each feature small enough that its work fits comfortably in a single context window — if an agent would have to COMPACT its context to finish, the feature is too big: SPLIT it into smaller features here, with the user, rather than leaving it for fleet planning. Prefer more, smaller features over few large ones; a narrow feature is finished in one window, fails in isolation, and can be re-dispatched on its own. Do NOT design the integration contracts here — that's the Plan/Structure stage. When EVERY feature is populated, present the set and let the USER confirm to complete the stage — never advance the stage yourself.
name: Features
blurb: The user-facing capabilities — each one a stream.
prompt:
Define the app's user-facing capabilities — the things a user DOES ("invite teammates", "export
to CSV"), never infrastructure (auth, queues, storage are implementation detail under a feature).
Each capability becomes its own fleet stream. Propose the COMPLETE set a production-grade solution
to the goal needs — not a minimal cut — then let the user curate it, and take each in turn.

substeps.label: Propose the feature set
substeps.prompt:
From the goal, scope, and what you've discussed, propose the COMPLETE set of user-facing
capabilities a production-grade solution to this goal needs — aim for the best, most complete
product, not a minimal first-pass cut. (Completeness is about capabilities, not
phasing — the user sequences them into phases next; don't pre-trim to a phase-1 slice.) Register the
WHOLE roster as titles in one pass — `bsc plan feature add "Invite teammates" "Export to CSV" …`
(names only; each appears in the Features board as an undefined title for the user to curate — add,
remove, merge, rename). Do NOT fill in any detail yet. Confirm the SET with the user before drilling
into any single feature.

substeps.label: Define each feature
substeps.prompt:
Now take ONE feature at a time. For THIS feature, fill in its detail by slug with
`echo '{"slug":"…","behavior":"…","acceptance":["…"],"approach":"…","tools":["…"],"data":"…"}' | bsc plan feature add`
(merges in place — do NOT resend the name):
• `behavior` + `acceptance` (a string array) — what it does, and the done-when checklist.
• `approach` — the concrete shape of the solution.
• `tools` (a string array) — the specific libraries/services/frameworks (name them).
• `data` — what it stores/reads.
• `dependsOn` — slugs of the OTHER features this one builds on (the roadmap DAG; keep it acyclic). A
feature may be foundational (others depend on it) — that's expected, not just user-facing capabilities.
• `requires` (a string array) — the ALGORITHM IDS from the shared library this capability needs, so the
building agent reuses the reference implementation instead of hand-rolling the same sort/traversal/diff
again. LOOK THEM UP FIRST with `bsc graph impl list` and name only ids you actually found — a guessed id
is a dangling reference. Omit it when nothing in the library applies; most features need none, and
inventing a match is worse than an empty list.
This feature is its own fleet STREAM (its slug). Propose, then interrogate with the user. Do NOT
design the integration contracts between features here — the Plan stage owns the seams. When EVERY
feature is populated, present the set and let the USER confirm the stage — do not advance yourself.
